full_judgment:
MR. MAINUR REZA CHOWDHURY, J:- This criminal petition for leave to appeal is against the judgment and order of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4807 of 1998 discharging the Rule. 

 2. The petitioner filed an application before the Golapganj Police Station, District Sylhet on 1.1.98 that case land originally a homestead now recorded into Charabari has been possessed by the petitioner growing fruits and vegetables but the 2nd party forming and unlawful assembly being armed with deadly weapon threatening the petitioner with dispossession respective in an apprehension of breach of peace over the case land and imminent danger to life and property. Whereupon the police submitted a prosecution report as to apprehension of breach of peace and considering the emergent situation recommended for attachment of the case land. On 22.2.98 the Magistrate registered a non-G.R. Case No. 3 of 1998 under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and issued notice upon the petitioner and the 2nd party fixing 10.2.1998. As none of the 2nd party appeared the case was adjourned to 16.2.1998 for written statement. On 16.2.1998 the first group of second party filed written statement while the 2nd group of second party did neither appeared nor filed written statement and on personal of the materials the learned Magistrate drew up a proceedings under section 145 Cr.P.C., attached the case land and appointed Assistant Commissioner (Land) Golapganj as the receiver of the property. The next date, the respondent-second party-second group filed a written statement and on application for vacating the order which was rejected by the learned Magistrate, the respondent-second party-second group this filed Criminal Motion No.70 of 1998 before the learned Sessions Judge who by the impugned order dated 21.7.98 allowed the Motion and set aside the order of attachment of the case land and appointment of receiver passed by the learned Magistrate, First Class, Sylhet. Against the said order the second party-First group moved the High Court Division. 

 4. Magistrate exercising jurisdiction under section 145 Cr. P.C. drawing up a proceeding could in an emergent situation attach the case land in order to prevent imminent preach of the peace. The 2nd proviso to section 145 Cr.P.C. authorizes the Magistrate to attach the subject matter of dispute at any time when he considered the case on of emergency and as such the Magistrate is required to record an emergent situation exists or existed for passing an order under the aforesaid provision.
